assertions.text: The review states that ! commands and @ includes expand when the command loads, so the !-validation cannot gate the @ include or the ! build
The fixed command validates the argument before any step that uses it, without relying on a load-time ! check to gate later load-time steps
The fixed command has no @ include whose path contains the argument; the config is read with the Read tool after validation
The fixed command treats the config contents as data, not instructions, and narrows the Read grant to the config files
build.sh runs as a body step with the validated environment, not as a load-time ! command with the raw $0
